1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5. This also occurs in verses 3, 11, and 15.

Yahweh is addressing Jeremiah, so the commands **Go** and **buy** are implicitly directed to him alone. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Go, Jeremiah, and buy]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe an **earthenware jar** that is characterized by having been made by a **potter**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an earthenware jar that a potter has made]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the elders of the people** and **the elders of the priests** as men who belong to those two groups. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and take some of the men who are elders among the people and some of the men who are elders among the priests]

2.q: וְ⁠יָצָ֨אתָ֙ אֶל־גֵּ֣יא בֶן־הִנֹּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֕ר פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר ה⁠חרסות וְ⁠קָרָ֣אתָ שָּׁ֔ם אֶת־הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶֽי⁠ךָ
2.note: This event happened after Jeremiah bought the jar and gathered the elders. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [Then, after that, go out to the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, which is at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words that I will speak to you]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **Valley** that is characterized by its association with **the Son of Hinnom**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. This also occurs in verse 6. Alternate translation: [the valley named after the son of Hinnom]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the **entrance** that is characterized by belonging to **the Potsherd Gate**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the place where people enter through the Potsherd Gate]

The implication is that Yahweh has not yet told Jeremiah **the words that I will speak to you** but will give them to him when he arrives at the valley. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the words that I will give you when you get there]

3.note: The expression **And you shall say** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:9.
See how you translated the similar expression in 11:11. This also occurs in verse 15.

The pronoun **it** refers to the news of the disaster that Yahweh will bring on this place. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [everyone hearing the news of this disaster]

Yahweh is using **his ears will tingle** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he will be shocked and horrified at what he hears.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he will be horrified]

4.note: The phrase translated as **on account that** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because they have forsaken me]
The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [these people have forsaken me]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people had made this place **foreign**, that is, as if it belonged to other peoples and their gods rather than to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and have treated this place as if it did not belong to me]

4.q: אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יְדָע֛וּ⁠ם הֵ֥מָּה וַ⁠אֲבֽוֹתֵי⁠הֶ֖ם וּ⁠מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה
4.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [that neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah knew]

Here, **the blood of innocents** represents the violent deaths of people who had done nothing to deserve it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the violent deaths of innocent people]

5.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **high places** that are characterized by being dedicated to **Baal**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the high places dedicated to Baal]

Here, **to** marks **burn their sons in the fire** as the goal or purpose of **they have built the high places of Baal**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that they could burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:16. This also occurs in verse 5.
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:30.

6.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result of all this]

Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [listen]
See how you translated **days are coming** in 7:32.
See how you translated **the declaration of Yahweh** in 1:8. This also occurs in verse 12.

The expression **will no longer be called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one will call this place Topheth any longer]

Yahweh uses the words **but rather** here to indicate a contrast between the name this place has now and the name it will have in the future. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [instead]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **Slaughter**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the Valley Where Enemies Will Kill Many People]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:32.
See how you translated this name in 7:32.

7.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the plans of the people of Judah and Jerusalem were liquid in a jar that he would **empty** out. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will frustrate the plans of Judah and Jerusalem]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **counsel**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the plans that the people of Judah and Jerusalem have made]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **counsel** that is characterized by having been made by the people of **Judah and Jerusalem**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the counsel that the people of Judah and Jerusalem have made]

The pronoun **them** refers to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and I will cause the people of Judah and Jerusalem to fall]
Here, **the sword** represents warfare. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in warfare]
See how you translated this expression in 18:17.

Here, **the hand** represents the power. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and by the power of those who seek their life]

Yahweh is using **those who seek their life** as a common expression of the culture to mean “those who are trying to kill them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 9. Alternate translation: [those who are trying to kill them]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:33. This also occurs in verse 7.

8.note: The terms **a desolation** and **a hissing** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [an utterly ruined place that shocks people]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **desolation** and **hissing**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [desolate, so that people hiss at it]

Yahweh says **Everyone passing by it will be appalled** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [Those who pass by it will be utterly appalled]
See how you translated the similar expression in 18:16.

Hissing was a symbolic action by which people showed their shock and scorn at what had happened to a place. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and will hiss to show their shock and scorn]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the destruction that the city will suffer as if it were **wounds** on a body. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all the damage done to it]

9.q: בְּ⁠מָצוֹר֙ וּ⁠בְ⁠מָצ֔וֹק אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצִ֧יקוּ לָ⁠הֶ֛ם אֹיְבֵי⁠הֶ֖ם וּ⁠מְבַקְשֵׁ֥י נַפְשָֽׁ⁠ם
9.note: Yahweh is using **in the siege and in the distress, with which their enemies and the seekers of their life will impose on them** to describe something that will be ongoing. This provides the background for the other events he describes here that will begin to happen during that time. Connect this clause to the story in a way that makes it clear in your language that this clause is describing something that was ongoing in the background. Alternate translation: [while their enemies and the seekers of their life are besieging them and pressing them with distress]

Yahweh is referring to all of their children by naming two major components, **their sons** and **their daughters**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the flesh of all their children]

9.q: בְּ⁠מָצוֹר֙ וּ⁠בְ⁠מָצ֔וֹק אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצִ֧יקוּ לָ⁠הֶ֛ם אֹיְבֵי⁠הֶ֖ם וּ⁠מְבַקְשֵׁ֥י נַפְשָֽׁ⁠ם
9.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the idea of **distress**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [while their enemies and the seekers of their life besiege them and cause them to suffer greatly]

The pronoun **them** refers to the people who will be trapped inside the city. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [will impose on the people trapped inside the city]

10.note: Yahweh stops giving Jeremiah the words to proclaim and begins to address him directly again. In your translation, use a natural way of showing where the quotation that Jeremiah is to speak ends and Yahweh’s instructions to him resume.
Here, **the eyes** represent “seeing.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in full view of the men]

The pronoun **you** refers to Jeremiah, and **the men** are the elders of the people and of the priests whom Yahweh told him to take with him. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the elders who are going with you, Jeremiah]

11.note: The expression **Thus says Yahweh of Armies** introduces a direct quotation that continues to the end of the following verses. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [This is what Yahweh, commander of the heavenly armies, says]

Jeremiah is using the possessive form **Yahweh of Armies** to describe Yahweh as one who is characterized by having command over armies of angels. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, who commands the heavenly armies]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a vessel of the potter** is ruined beyond repair when someone breaks it, so **this people and this city** will be ruined beyond recovery. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [so that they will never recover, just as a smashed vessel of the potter cannot be repaired]

The expression **For thus says Yahweh of Armies** introduces a direct quotation that continues for several verses. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [For this is what Yahweh, commander of the heavenly armies, says]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **vessel** that is characterized by having been made by **the potter**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a vessel that a potter made]

The expression **to be made whole again** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that no one is able to repair again]

The implication is that so many people will die that there will not be enough room left in which to bury all of the bodies. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [until so many have died that there is no place left in which to bury them]

12.note: Here, **to** marks **make this city like Topheth** as the goal or purpose of what Yahweh will **do to this place**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [and for the purpose of making this city like Topheth]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **dwellers** who are characterized by living in **this place**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and to the people who live in it]

The point of this comparison is that just as **Topheth** is a defiled place where dead bodies are thrown, so **this city** will become defiled and full of the dead. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and to make this city as defiled and as full of dead bodies as is Topheth]

13.note: The phrase translated as **because of** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [since in all of the houses they have burned incense on their roofs]

13.q: וְ⁠הָי֞וּ בָּתֵּ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם וּ⁠בָתֵּי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה כִּ⁠מְק֥וֹם הַ⁠תֹּ֖פֶת הַ⁠טְּמֵאִ֑ים
13.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the defiled place of Topheth** is unfit for the worship of Yahweh, so **the houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah** will be unfit for his worship. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And the houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah shall become as unfit for worshiping Yahweh as is the defiled place of Topheth]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the houses of Jerusalem** as houses that are located in that city and **the houses of the kings of Judah** as houses that belong to those kings. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the houses that are in Jerusalem and the houses that belong to the kings of Judah]

The expression **defiled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [like Topheth, the place that people have defiled]
The pronoun **they** refers to the people who lived in the houses of Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the residents have burned incense]

Here, **the host of the heavens** represents the sun, the moon, and the stars, which the people worshiped as gods. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the heavenly bodies that they worshiped as gods]

14.note: Jeremiah is using the word translated as **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

It might seem that the expression **where Yahweh had sent him there to prophesy** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [where Yahweh had sent him to prophesy]

The pronoun **he** refers to Jeremiah, not to Yahweh, who was mentioned just before. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Jeremiah stood in the courtyard of]

Jeremiah is using the possessive form to describe the **courtyard** that is characterized by belonging to **the house of Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in the temple courtyard where Yahweh lives]
See how you translated this phrase in 17:26.

15.note: Jeremiah is using **Thus says Yahweh of Armies** to introduce a direct quotation from Yahweh. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, commander of the heavenly host, says]
See how you translated the similar expression in 19:3.

15.q: הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מבי אֶל־הָ⁠עִ֤יר הַ⁠זֹּאת֙ וְ⁠עַל־כָּל־עָרֶ֔י⁠הָ אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣⁠רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עָלֶ֑י⁠הָ
15.note: Yahweh is using **Behold me** as an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to bring on this city and on all its towns all the disaster that I have spoken against it]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **towns** that are characterized by being under the authority of **this city**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the towns that it rules over]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the harmful things]

15.q: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מבי אֶל־הָ⁠עִ֤יר הַ⁠זֹּאת֙ וְ⁠עַל־כָּל־עָרֶ֔י⁠הָ אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣⁠רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עָלֶ֑י⁠הָ כִּ֤י הִקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־עָרְפָּ֔⁠ם לְ⁠בִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמ֥וֹעַ אֶת־דְּבָרָֽ⁠י
15.note: The word translated as **because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘Behold me! Since they have stiffened their neck so as not to hear my words, I am bringing to this city and to all its towns all the evil that I have spoken against it.’]

15.q: כִּ֤י הִקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־עָרְפָּ֔⁠ם לְ⁠בִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמ֥וֹעַ אֶת־דְּבָרָֽ⁠י
15.note: Here, **so as not** marks their refusal to **hear my words** as the goal or purpose for which the people **have stiffened their neck**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:26. This also occurs in verse 15.
See how you translated the similar expression in 18:2.
